195: /// Removes surrounding quotes from a string. Doesn't remove quotes from raw
196: /// strings. Returns the original string if it doesn't have matching quotes.
197: fn remove_quotes(s: &str) -> &str {
198:     let quoted_by_double_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('"') && s.ends_with('"');
199:     let quoted_by_single_quotes = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('\'') && s.ends_with('\'');
200:     let quoted_by_backticks = s.len() >= 2 && s.starts_with('`') && s.ends_with('`');
201:     if quoted_by_double_quotes || quoted_by_single_quotes || quoted_by_backticks {
202:         &s[1..s.len() - 1]
203:     } else {
204:         s
205:     }
206: }

208: /// Evaluate all arguments from a call, performing expansions when necessary.
209: pub fn eval_arguments_from_call(
210:     engine_state: &EngineState,
211:     stack: &mut Stack,
212:     call: &Call,
213: ) -> Result<Vec<Spanned<String>>, ShellError> {
214:     let cwd = engine_state.cwd(Some(stack))?;
215:     let mut args: Vec<Spanned<String>> = vec![];
216:     for (expr, spread) in call.rest_iter(1) {
217:         if is_bare_string(expr) {
218:             // If `expr` is a bare string, perform tilde-expansion,
219:             // glob-expansion, and inner-quotes-removal, in that order.
220:             let glob_expander = ExternalGlob {
221:                 strip_working_directory: true,
222:                 keep_unmatched_pattern: true,
223:             };
224:             for arg in eval_argument(engine_state, stack, expr, spread)? {
225:                 let tilde_expanded = expand_tilde(&arg);
226:                 let glob = GlobExpansion::new(tilde_expanded, &cwd, expr.span);
227:                 for glob_expanded in glob_expander.expand_glob(&glob)? {
228:                     let inner_quotes_removed = remove_inner_quotes(&glob_expanded);
229:                     args.push(inner_quotes_removed.into_owned().into_spanned(expr.span));
230:                 }
231:             }
232:         } else {
233:             for arg in eval_argument(engine_state, stack, expr, spread)? {
234:                 args.push(arg.into_spanned(expr.span));
235:             }
236:         }
237:     }
238:     Ok(args)
239: }

241: /// Evaluates an expression, coercing the values to strings.
242: ///
243: /// Note: The parser currently has a special hack that retains surrounding
244: /// quotes for string literals in `Expression`, so that we can decide whether
245: /// the expression is considered a bare string. The hack doesn't affect string
246: /// literals within lists or records. This function will remove the quotes
247: /// before evaluating the expression.
248: fn eval_argument(
249:     engine_state: &EngineState,
250:     stack: &mut Stack,
251:     expr: &Expression,
252:     spread: bool,
253: ) -> Result<Vec<String>, ShellError> {
254:     // Remove quotes from string literals.
255:     let mut expr = expr.clone();
256:     if let Expr::String(s) = &expr.expr {
257:         expr.expr = Expr::String(remove_quotes(s).into());
258:     }
259: 
260:     let eval = get_eval_expression(engine_state);
261:     match eval(engine_state, stack, &expr)? {
262:         Value::List { vals, .. } => {
263:             if spread {
264:                 vals.into_iter()
265:                     .map(|val| val.coerce_into_string())
266:                     .collect()
267:             } else {
268:                 Err(ShellError::CannotPassListToExternal {
269:                     arg: String::from_utf8_lossy(engine_state.get_span_contents(expr.span)).into(),
270:                     span: expr.span,
271:                 })
272:             }
273:         }
274:         value => {
275:             if spread {
276:                 Err(ShellError::CannotSpreadAsList { span: expr.span })
277:             } else {
278:                 Ok(vec![value.coerce_into_string()?])
279:             }
280:         }
281:     }
282: }

323:         let Ok(paths) = nu_glob::glob_with_parent(pattern, options, cwd) else {
324:             return Ok(vec![pattern.into()]);

330:                 msg: format!("{}: {:?}", err.path().display(), err.error()),
331:                 span: glob.span,

334:             let path_stripped = if self.strip_working_directory {
335:                 path.strip_prefix(cwd).unwrap_or(&path)

360: /// Transforms `--option="value"` into `--option=value`. `value` can be quoted
361: /// with double quotes, single quotes, or backticks. Only removes the outermost
362: /// pair of quotes after the equal sign.
363: fn remove_inner_quotes(arg: &str) -> Cow<'_, str> {
364:     // Check that `arg` is a long option.
365:     if !arg.starts_with("--") {
366:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
367:     }
368:     // Split `arg` on the first `=`.
369:     let Some((option, value)) = arg.split_once('=') else {
370:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
371:     };
372:     // Check that `option` doesn't contain quotes.
373:     if option.contains('"') || option.contains('\'') || option.contains('`') {
374:         return Cow::Borrowed(arg);
375:     }
376:     // Remove the outermost pair of quotes from `value`.
377:     let value = remove_quotes(value);
378:     Cow::Owned(format!("{option}={value}"))
379: }

381: /// Write `PipelineData` into `writer`. If `PipelineData` is not binary, it is
382: /// first rendered using the `table` command.
383: ///
384: /// Note: Avoid using this function when piping data from an external command to
385: /// another external command, because it copies data unnecessarily. Instead,
386: /// extract the pipe from the `PipelineData::ByteStream` of the first command
387: /// and hand it to the second command directly.
388: fn write_pipeline_data(
389:     mut engine_state: EngineState,
390:     mut stack: Stack,
391:     data: PipelineData,
392:     mut writer: impl Write,
393: ) -> Result<(), ShellError> {
394:     if let PipelineData::ByteStream(stream, ..) = data {
395:         stream.write_to(writer)?;
396:     } else if let PipelineData::Value(Value::Binary { val, .. }, ..) = data {
397:         writer.write_all(&val)?;
398:     } else {
399:         stack.start_capture();
400: 
401:         // Turn off color as we pass data through
402:         Arc::make_mut(&mut engine_state.config).use_ansi_coloring = false;
403: 
404:         // Invoke the `table` command.
405:         let output =
406:             crate::Table.run(&engine_state, &mut stack, &Call::new(Span::unknown()), data)?;
407: 
408:         // Write the output.
409:         for value in output {
410:             let bytes = value.coerce_into_binary()?;
411:             writer.write_all(&bytes)?;
412:         }
413:     }
414:     Ok(())
415: }

417: /// Returns a helpful error message given an invalid command name,
418: pub fn command_not_found(
419:     name: &str,
420:     span: Span,
421:     engine_state: &EngineState,
422:     stack: &mut Stack,
423: ) -> ShellError {
424:     // Run the `command_not_found` hook if there is one.
425:     if let Some(hook) = &engine_state.config.hooks.command_not_found {
426:         let mut stack = stack.start_capture();
427:         // Set a special environment variable to avoid infinite loops when the
428:         // `command_not_found` hook triggers itself.
429:         let canary = "ENTERED_COMMAND_NOT_FOUND";
430:         if stack.has_env_var(engine_state, canary) {
431:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
432:                 label: format!(
433:                     "Command {name} not found while running the `command_not_found` hook"
434:                 ),
435:                 help: "Make sure the `command_not_found` hook itself does not use unknown commands"
436:                     .into(),
437:                 span,
438:             };
439:         }
440:         stack.add_env_var(canary.into(), Value::bool(true, Span::unknown()));
441: 
442:         let output = eval_hook(
443:             &mut engine_state.clone(),
444:             &mut stack,
445:             None,
446:             vec![("cmd_name".into(), Value::string(name, span))],
447:             hook,
448:             "command_not_found",
449:         );
450: 
451:         // Remove the special environment variable that we just set.
452:         stack.remove_env_var(engine_state, canary);
453: 
454:         match output {
455:             Ok(PipelineData::Value(Value::String { val, .. }, ..)) => {
456:                 return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
457:                     label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
458:                     help: val,
459:                     span,
460:                 };
461:             }
462:             Err(err) => {
463:                 return err;
464:             }
465:             _ => {
466:                 // The hook did not return a string, so ignore it.
467:             }
468:         }
469:     }
470: 
471:     // If the name is one of the removed commands, recommend a replacement.
472:     if let Some(replacement) = crate::removed_commands().get(&name.to_lowercase()) {
473:         return ShellError::RemovedCommand {
474:             removed: name.to_lowercase(),
475:             replacement: replacement.clone(),
476:             span,
477:         };
478:     }
479: 
480:     // The command might be from another module. Try to find it.
481:     if let Some(module) = engine_state.which_module_has_decl(name.as_bytes(), &[]) {
482:         let module = String::from_utf8_lossy(module);
483:         // Is the command already imported?
484:         let full_name = format!("{module} {name}");
485:         if engine_state.find_decl(full_name.as_bytes(), &[]).is_some() {
486:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
487:                 label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
488:                 help: format!("Did you mean `{full_name}`?"),
489:                 span,
490:             };
491:         } else {
492:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
493:                 label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
494:                 help: format!("A command with that name exists in module `{module}`. Try importing it with `use`"),
495:                 span,
496:             };
497:         }
498:     }
499: 
500:     // Try to match the name with the search terms of existing commands.
501:     let signatures = engine_state.get_signatures(false);
502:     if let Some(sig) = signatures.iter().find(|sig| {
503:         sig.search_terms
504:             .iter()
505:             .any(|term| term.to_folded_case() == name.to_folded_case())
506:     }) {
507:         return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
508:             label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
509:             help: format!("Did you mean `{}`?", sig.name),
510:             span,
511:         };
512:     }
513: 
514:     // Try a fuzzy search on the names of all existing commands.
515:     if let Some(cmd) = did_you_mean(signatures.iter().map(|sig| &sig.name), name) {
516:         // The user is invoking an external command with the same name as a
517:         // built-in command. Remind them of this.
518:         if cmd == name {
519:             return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
520:                 label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
521:                 help: "There is a built-in command with the same name".into(),
522:                 span,
523:             };
524:         }
525:         return ShellError::ExternalCommand {
526:             label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
527:             help: format!("Did you mean `{cmd}`?"),
528:             span,
529:         };
530:     }
531: 
532:     // We found nothing useful. Give up and return a generic error message.
533:     ShellError::ExternalCommand {
534:         label: format!("Command `{name}` not found"),
535:         help: format!("`{name}` is neither a Nushell built-in or a known external command"),
536:         span,
537:     }
538: }

540: /// Searches for the absolute path of an executable by name. `.bat` and `.cmd`

542: ///
543: /// This is a wrapper around `which::which_in()` except that, on Windows, it
544: /// also searches the current directory before any PATH entries.

546: /// Note: the `which.rs` crate always uses PATHEXT from the environment. As
547: /// such, changing PATHEXT within Nushell doesn't work without updating the
548: /// actual environment of the Nushell process.

556: /// list can be found at https://ss64.com/nt/syntax-internal.html
557: fn is_cmd_internal_command(name: &str) -> bool {
558:     const COMMANDS: &[&str] = &[
559:         "ASSOC", "CLS", "ECHO", "FTYPE", "MKLINK", "PAUSE", "START", "VER", "VOL",
560:     ];
561:     COMMANDS.iter().any(|cmd| cmd.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))

566: fn has_cmd_special_character(s: &str) -> bool {
567:     const SPECIAL_CHARS: &[char] = &['<', '>', '&', '|', '^'];

571: /// Escape an argument for CMD internal commands. The result can be safely
572: /// passed to `raw_arg()`.
573: #[cfg(windows)]
574: fn escape_cmd_argument(arg: &Spanned<String>) -> Result<Cow<'_, str>, ShellError> {
575:     let Spanned { item: arg, span } = arg;
576:     if arg.contains('"') {
577:         // If `arg` is already quoted by double quotes, confirm there's no
578:         // embedded double quotes, then leave it as is.
579:         if arg.chars().filter(|c| *c == '"').count() == 2
580:             && arg.starts_with('"')
581:             && arg.ends_with('"')
582:         {
583:             Ok(Cow::Borrowed(arg))
584:         } else {
585:             Err(ShellError::ExternalCommand {
586:                 label: "Arguments to CMD internal commands cannot contain embedded double quotes"
587:                     .into(),
588:                 help: "CMD doesn't support escaping double quotes inside double quotes".into(),
589:                 span: *span,
590:             })
591:         }
592:     } else if arg.contains(' ') || has_cmd_special_character(arg) {
593:         // If `arg` contains space or special characters, quote the entire argument by double quotes.
594:         Ok(Cow::Owned(format!("\"{arg}\"")))
595:     } else {
596:         Ok(Cow::Borrowed(arg))
597:     }
598: }
